title: First-to-third grip changes do not improve cross-cycle HbA1c prediction beyond peak strength
abstract: Among NHANES adults aged >=40 with complete bilateral grip trials, adding first-to-third grip changes to a peak-strength and anthropometric model did not improve frozen 2011-12 to 2013-14 HbA1c prediction: weighted MSE gain -0.002947 percentage-points squared (conditional 95% stratified-PSU bootstrap interval -0.006687 to 0.000475); target RMSE was 1.006687 versus 1.008150 percentage points in 3,162 participants. This negative model comparison concerns three rested maximal trials, not a validated fatigue protocol or a diagnostic test. Separate survey samples establish only temporal within-platform transfer; the interval does not exclude a small gain.
